children: According to CNBC, Matthews Asia portfolio manager Andrew Mattock said investors seeking greater artificial intelligence exposure should focus on China rather than broad emerging market funds. He said standard emerging market strategies and plain-vanilla MSCI products do not provide much exposure to Chinese AI names, and noted that South Korean and Taiwanese companies make up almost half of the iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (EEM) while the iShares MSCI China ETF (MCHI) lacks a focus on AI stocks. Mattock manages the Matthews China Fund (MCHFX), which invests at least 80% of its net assets in common and preferred stocks of companies located in China, according to the firm's website. The fund was down 4% for the year as of Friday's close, and its largest holdings include Tencent and Alibaba. The article also said billionaire hedge fund manager David Tepper told CNBC in September 2024 that he bought more of "everything" related to China, while KraneShares chief investment officer Brendan Ahern said investors could use options around ETFs such as KWEB to help protect against sharp swings in China. According to FactSet, the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF shares Tencent and Alibaba as its top two holdings and was down more than 27% for the year as of Friday's close.

title: Matthews Asia's Andrew Mattock Says Investors Should Target China for AI Exposure
